events.stem:
Treatment of NO₃⁻ with Zn or Al in conc. NaOH on warming produces the N-containing product <L>. Reaction of <L> with O₂ in the presence of Pt catalyst at high temperature yields the N-containing product <M>.
Choose the correct option(s).
(A) N in <L> is sp³ hybridised
(B) The number of unpaired electrons in <M> is 0
(C) The bond order of <M> is 2.5
(D) The shape of <L> is trigonal pyramidal

inputs.statement: The number of unpaired electrons in <M> is 0
The shape of <L> is trigonal pyramidal

Treatment of NO3- with Zn or Al in conc. NaOH on warming produces nitrite (NO2-) or nitrosyl complex? Typical reaction: NO3- + 2Al + 3H2O → Al(OH)3 + NO2-? Actually Al reduces NO3- to NO2- in basic medium. Zn also reduces. So <L> likely nitrite ion NO2- (N in NO2- is sp2 hybridised? NO2- has bent shape trigonal? N in NO2- is sp2 hybridised with one lone pair, shape bent. But option D says trigonal pyramidal, which is for e.g. NH3 or NO3-? NO3- is trigonal planar. However nitrite ion is bent (approx 134°). Trigonal pyramidal would be for e.g. NH2-? Not correct. Option A says N in <L> is sp3 hybridised – NO2- uses sp2. So A false. Option D false.
Reaction of <L> with O2 in presence of Pt catalyst at high temperature yields N-containing product <M>. Likely NO2 (nitrogen dioxide) or NO? Pt catalyst reduces NO2 to NO? High temperature oxidation of nitrite could give NO2? Actually NO2 + O2? Might give NO3? But typical oxidation of NO2- to NO3-? However Pt catalyst at high T could produce NO (nitric oxide) with bond order 2.5 (NO bond order 2.5). NO has bond order 2.5 (diatomic). So <M> could be NO. NO has no unpaired electrons (all paired? NO has one unpaired electron? NO radical has one unpaired electron. Wait NO has 11 electrons, one unpaired. But NO+ has no unpaired. However NO2+ has no unpaired? NO2+ (nitronium) has bond order 2.5? Actually NO2+ bond order 2.5? NO2+ has bond order 2.5? NO2+ is isoelectronic with CO, bond order 2.5? CO bond order 3? No CO bond order 3. NO2+ has bond order 2.5? Let's recall: NO2 radical has bond order 2, NO2+ has bond order 2.5, NO2- has bond order 1.5. So <M> likely NO2+ (nitronium) formed by oxidation of NO2- with O2 and Pt catalyst. Nitronium ion NO2+ has no unpaired electrons (all paired), bond order 2.5. So B true (0 unpaired), C true (bond order 2.5). D false, A false. Thus correct options B and C.

members.working: NO₃⁻ reduced by Zn/Al in conc. NaOH gives ammonia (NH₃) = <L>. NH₃ with O₂ over Pt at high temperature (Ostwald process) gives NO = <M>. (A) N in NH₃ is sp³ hybridised — correct. (B) NO has 11 valence electrons (odd), so it has 1 unpaired electron — incorrect. (C) Bond order of NO = (10−5)/2 = 2.5 — correct. (D) NH₃ is trigonal pyramidal — correct.
